title: Aniimo Currencies And Glimmer Guide | How To Earn And Spend Without Wasting | Aniimo Guide
description: A simple guide to the Aniimo economy: what Credits, Glimmer, Lumin Crystals and Primegy are for, every free way to earn Glimmer, the best things to spend it on and what to skip. Checked against several guides in November 2026; amounts and shop prices can change with patches, so check the in-game listing.

thumbnail.text: GLIMMER: EARN IT, SPEND IT RIGHT

sections.heading: Understanding the Aniimo economy
sections.script: Aniimo does not have one universal wallet. It has many currencies, and most of them only work inside one system. That confuses new players, and it leads to wasted resources. In this video we focus on the ones that matter the most. Credits, which you use all the time. Glimmer, the scarce one. Lumin Crystals, the premium one. And Primegy, your stamina. Then we cover every free way to earn Glimmer, what is actually worth buying with it, and what to avoid. The guides we checked agree on the big picture, but exact amounts and prices can differ and change with patches, so always check the number shown in your own game. Think of the economy as a set of small pockets rather than one big wallet. Money earned in one pocket rarely moves into another, so the skill is knowing which pocket to fill, and which one to leave alone. Beginners who understand this early always feel richer than players who do not.

sections.heading: The four currencies that matter
sections.script: Let us sort the big four. Credits are your everyday money. You earn them through normal play, like catch reports, chests and quests, and you spend them on things like Aniipods and general vendor stock. Glimmer is the harder currency. It has fewer sources, so it is worth managing carefully, and it pays for higher tier shop items and refills. Lumin Crystals are the premium currency, and guides describe them as mainly for outfits and convenience, bought with real money. Finally Primegy is stamina. You spend it to claim rewards like boss chests and it comes back over time. Keep that picture in mind, and the rest becomes easy.

sections.heading: Credits: the easy money
sections.script: Credits are easier to earn than Glimmer, so you should never feel stuck on them. Guides point to catch reports as a steady income, along with chests, quests and Aniilog levels. Rarity matters, so a perfect catch pays much better than a common one. Because Credits are easy to farm, the golden rule is simple. If something can be bought with Credits, do not pay Glimmer for it. Common Aniipods are a perfect example. Check the daily offer in the shop first, because discounted stock is cheaper than the standard price. Use Credits for your routine needs, and keep your Glimmer for things Credits cannot buy. Remember also that releasing creatures you no longer need can return useful leveling materials, so a cleaned up roster helps your wallet too, not only your menu.

sections.heading: Free Glimmer: the big milestones
sections.script: Now the interesting part, free Glimmer. Several guides agree on these rewards. Defeating an Alpha Aniimo for the first time gives fifty Glimmer. Defeating an Omega for the first time gives one hundred. Both are one time rewards, so repeat kills do not pay again. Even better, every Aniilog research level you gain rewards one hundred Glimmer, and you earn research by catching Aniimo, their different forms, and completing research goals. Remember to submit your research at an Outpost first. This is why catching widely early on is a smart move. The more you collect, the higher your research level climbs, and the more Glimmer you collect along with it. So the best early habit is to open your Aniilog often, check which research goals are close, and finish them on your way. Those hundred Glimmer rewards add up faster than almost any other source, and they cost you nothing but time spent playing the game you already enjoy.

sections.heading: Free Glimmer: daily and story sources
sections.script: Beyond the milestones, there are steady sources. The Daily Activity page in the Institute Guide is the one reliable daily source. Complete the listed tasks, collect activity points, and claim the Glimmer reward for the day. Guides mention a milestone of four hundred points. Story progress helps as well, through chapter quests and the Elite Training core courses, though those are limited, one time rewards. Region branch quests, chests in caves after puzzles, and active gift codes can add more. The amounts vary from guide to guide, so we will not quote them. The takeaway is that free Glimmer exists, but it is finite, so spend it with a plan.

sections.heading: What to buy first: Primegy refills
sections.script: So where should Glimmer go? Guides agree on one safe use. Refilling Primegy. A refill costs around fifty Glimmer in the guides we read. That sounds like a lot, but late in the game it can keep you farming Alpha and Omega bosses and simulator runs when your stamina is empty. The advice is to keep a small buffer for those moments. Do not refill constantly early on, because Primegy also comes back for free over time. Think of this purchase as a tool for busy days, not as a daily habit. If you spend your stamina every session as you play, you will rarely need to refill at all. Your Homeland and your daily tasks also give you a reason to log in every day, and that steady routine is worth more than any single purchase.

sections.heading: Capafruit and Sparkling Cubes
sections.script: Two items tempt a lot of players. The first is Capafruit. It costs about one thousand Glimmer and gives a permanent boost to Innate Potential. Guides say to buy it only once your core team is settled, because it is expensive and you do not want to put it into an Aniimo you will replace. The second is the Sparkling Cube, a capture item that guarantees a catch with Sparkling status and perfect stats. You collect Sparkling Crystals from play, and the shop sells more for Glimmer under a weekly limit. Prices differ between guides, so check the shop. The rule for both is patience. Save them for creatures you plan to keep.

sections.heading: What to avoid
sections.script: Let us finish the practical part with the traps. Exchanges in this game are almost always irreversible, so read the destination and the amount before you confirm. For example, turning Glimmer into Fashion Vouchers cannot be reversed. Do not spend Glimmer on things you can farm with Credits. Do not rush Capafruit while you are still building your roster. And do not plan your whole economy around buying Lumin Crystals. Guides say free methods cover most needs. One more tip is to keep a little currency for event shops, because limited offers do not come back. Spend limited stock first, and unlimited materials later.

sections.heading: A simple weekly plan
sections.script: Here is an easy plan to follow. Every day, finish your Daily Activity and spend your Primegy before it caps. Every session, catch widely, because catching feeds research and research feeds Glimmer. Each time you level up your Aniilog, collect the reward. Take down new Alphas and Omegas for their first clear bonus. Use Credits for pods and normal supplies, and keep Glimmer for Primegy refills and one big upgrade at a time. Following these steps costs no real money, and it keeps your resources flowing in the right direction. Small habits like these are what separate a comfortable account from one that always feels poor. At the end of each week, look at what you have left over. If your Glimmer is climbing, you are doing it right, and you can afford the one big purchase you have been planning.

sections.heading: Your turn
sections.script: That is how the Aniimo economy works, and how to stay ahead of it. Prices and rewards can change with patches, so check the listings in your game. Now we want to hear from you. What do you spend your Glimmer on first? Capafruit, Sparkling Cubes, or Primegy refills? Share your pick in the comments. If this guide helped, please subscribe to HarryBeast Gaming for more Aniimo guides and updates, and we will see you in the next video.
